content:
maria: quick heads-up — legal asked for per-tenant signed audit exports covering 90d for a compliance review. asking how feasible to do a backfill + one-off download without blowing export quotas. :eyes:
akash: are they asking full event stream or compact change summaries?
taylor: compact ndjson with actor resolution would be fine. legal wants 'who changed what and when' with proof links.
elaine: main risk is rehydrating actor metadata. we currently drop heavy actor payloads from long-retention exports to save space. backfill will need walker job to resolve historical actor ids -> names.
akash: ok. two things: 1) residency/quota for heavy downloads — we have export_quota per-tenant (50GB/day) 2) can we route backfill jobs to Dedicated capacity to avoid throttling hosted?
infra-bot: deploy queued: export-backfill-worker v3.2 scheduled to staging at 1754322500.
maria: ideally we avoid Dedicated for ad-hoc legal requests. customers on hosted shouldn't pay extra by default. can we burst to background workers with throttling and priority so it doesn't affect real-time exports?
taylor: we can implement a 'rehydration' job type that streams compact events and lazily fetches actor snapshots from actor-store. that means extra I/O but keeps main export path unchanged.
elaine: question: where do we keep signatures? signed-proof is generated at export time using key-version id. if we rehydrate later, the key used may differ (rotations). legal requires signatures verifiable to time of event. we need signing-at-source or signing proof packaging.
akash: propose flow: 1) generate compact event ndjson, 2) fetch actor-resolution snapshots as separate manifest, 3) include signing-manifest with key-id and signature for each bundle. this allows verification even if KMS rotated.
sre-ops: how about quotas + UX: console should show an 'export backfill' request form that warns about quota impact and estimated time. include checkbox for 'dedicated-burst' (billable) vs 'throttled-hosted' (free but slower).
maria: yes — console should also allow picking sampling rate (full vs compact) and whether to include full payloads. default to compact.
taylor: small prototyping notes: we need API endpoint POST /audit_exports with body {tenant_id, start_ts, end_ts, mode: compact|full, rehydrate_actors: bool, priority: low|high, destination:webhook|presigned}. returns job_id.
akash: internally route high-priority to dedicated-pool if tenant has reserved capacity, else to burst queue with strict concurrency per-tenant. fallback to persisted ndjson in S3.
elaine: edge-case: actor deleted and not in actor-store snapshot retention. we need a 'best-effort' marker and include actor-hash with pseudonymized display and a 'actor_missing' flag in output. legal asked for evidence of attempts to resolve — add list of resolution-steps in metadata.
maria: can we estimate cost? if we rehydrate 90 days at 2GB/day events for tenant X -> 180GB raw, actor lookups add ~10%. so expect ~200GB work. console should provide estimate before starting.
sre-ops: operationally: add quota guard that prevents >2 concurrent heavy backfills per region and per-tenant daily cap of 500GB by default. allow override via enterprise support ticket.
akash: agree. implement rollouts: start with internal QA tenant, then staging for small customers, then canary to 5 tenants, metric: export-latency, host-cpu, s3-e2e-time.
taylor: for telemetry: emit events: export.requested, export.started, export.chunk_uploaded, export.completed, export.signature_mismatch. tag with job_id and tenant_id. hook alerts on signature_mismatch rate >0.1%.
elaine: console wire: add 'proof status' column in export history linking to pre-signed proof bundle and showing key-id used.
maria: ok next steps: akash + taylor to draft API shape and quota policy, elaine to write signing/backfill constraints doc, sre-ops to propose throttles and dashboards. i'll file a follow-up with owners. :white_check_mark:
akash: I'll put a PR draft up with the POST /audit_exports shape and quota checks by EOD.
taylor: will mock console UX screens and a telemetry spec.
elaine: I'll outline KMS/signing edge cases and sample manifest schema.
sre-ops: will add initial dashboard panels for export backfill concurrency and S3 throughput.
maria: thanks team. ping me when mocks + PR are ready.
